```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
```

```{python}
health_expenditure_wide = pd.read_csv(
    r"C:/Users/USER/Desktop/graph_courses _python/misc_public-main/misc_public-main/current_health_expenditure.csv",
    engine="python",          # more flexible parser
    on_bad_lines="skip"       # skips problematic rows
)

# HIV prevelence data
hiv_data = pd.read_csv(
    r"C:/Users/USER\Desktop/graph_courses _python/ddf--datapoints--estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49--by--country--year.csv",
    engine="python"
)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

# Convert column names to lowercase and remove spaces
hiv_data.columns = hiv_data.columns.str.lower().str.strip()

print("HIV columns after cleaning:")
print(hiv_data.columns.tolist())


# Rename country column if necessary
if "country name" in hiv_data.columns:
    hiv_data = hiv_data.rename(
        columns={"country name": "country"}
    )

elif "country" not in hiv_data.columns:
    # Use the first column as country if no country column exists
    hiv_data = hiv_data.rename(
        columns={hiv_data.columns[0]: "country"}
    )


# Clean country names
hiv_data["country"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
)


# Create a readable country label
hiv_data["country_label"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .str.replace("_", " ", regex=False)
    .str.title()
)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

# Country-name differences between the HIV dataset # and the health expenditure dataset
country_map = {
    "bahamas": "Bahamas,  The",
    "cape_verde": "Cabo Verde",
    "congo_rep": "Congo,  Rep.",
    "cote_d_ivoire": "Cote d'Ivoire",
    "egypt": "Egypt,  Arab Rep.",
    "gambia": "Gambia,  The",
    "guinea_bissau": "Guinea-Bissau",
    "iran": "Iran,  Islamic Rep.",
    "lao": "Lao PDR",
    "sao_tome_and_principe": "Sao Tome and Principe",
    "south_korea": "Korea,  Rep.",
    "swaziland": "Eswatini",
    "trinidad_and_tobago": "Trinidad and Tobago",
    "turkey": "Turkiye",
    "venezuela": "Venezuela,  RB",
    "yemen": "Yemen,  Rep.",
}


# Create a World Bank-compatible country name
hiv_data["wb_name"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .map(country_map)
    .fillna(hiv_data["country"].str.replace("_", " ", regex=False).str.title())
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false

# Find columns containing years
year_columns = [
    column for column in health_expenditure_wide.columns if str(column).isdigit()
]

print("Year columns found:")
print(year_columns[:10])


# Convert from wide format to long format
health_expenditure_long = health_expenditure_wide.melt(
    id_vars=["Country Name", "Country Code", "Indicator Name", "Indicator Code"],
    value_vars=year_columns,
    var_name="year",
    value_name="health_expenditure",
)


# Convert year to numeric
health_expenditure_long["year"] = pd.to_numeric(
    health_expenditure_long["year"], errors="coerce"
)


# Convert health expenditure to numeric
health_expenditure_long["health_expenditure"] = pd.to_numeric(
    health_expenditure_long["health_expenditure"], errors="coerce"
)


print(health_expenditure_long.head())
```

```{python}
#| echo: false

hiv_data["year"] = pd.to_numeric(
    hiv_data["year"],
    errors="coerce"
)

hiv_data["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"] = pd.to_numeric(
    hiv_data["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"],

)
```

```{python}

        "health_expenditure"

```

# Overview 

## Project Overview 

<div class="intro-box"> 
### HIV Prevalence, Health Expenditure & ARV Treatment HIV remains an important public health and health-security concern, particularly in countries where health systems face challenges in prevention, testing, treatment, and long-term care. Adequate health financing is important for strengthening health services, including HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and access to antiretroviral (ARV) therapy. This dashboard explores HIV prevalence among people aged 15–49 and current health expenditure per capita across countries and over time. It examines HIV trends, differences in health-system investment, geographical patterns, and the relationship between HIV prevalence and health expenditure. The analysis uses Python, Pandas, NumPy, and Plotly to clean, analyse, and visualise publicly available health data. 

</div>

# HIV Prevalence Analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false

hiv_trend = ( hiv_data .groupby("year", as_index=False) ["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"] .mean() .dropna() )
```

```{python}
fig_hiv_trend = px.line(
    hiv_trend,
    x="year",
    y="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    markers=True,
    title="Average HIV Prevalence Among People Aged 15–49 Over Time",
    labels={
        "year": "Year",
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)"
    }
)

fig_hiv_trend.update_layout(
    height=500,
    xaxis_title="Year",
    yaxis_title="HIV prevalence (%)"
)

fig_hiv_trend.show()
```

```{python}
top_hiv_plot = top_hiv.sort_values(
    "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49", ascending=True
)

fig_hiv_top10 = px.bar(
    top_hiv_plot,
    x="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    y="country_label",
    orientation="h",
    title=f"Top 10 Countries by HIV Prevalence ({hiv_latest_year})",
    labels={
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)",
        "country_label": "Country",
    },
    text="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
)

fig_hiv_top10.update_traces(texttemplate="%{text:.1f}%", textposition="outside")

fig_hiv_top10.update_layout(
    height=550, yaxis_title="Country", xaxis_title="HIV prevalence (%)"
)

fig_hiv_top10.show()
```


```{python}
fig_hiv_map = px.choropleth(
    hiv_latest_data,
    locations="country",
    locationmode="country names",
    color="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    hover_name="country_label",
    title=f"Global HIV Prevalence Among Ages 15–49 ({hiv_latest_year})",
    labels={"estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)"},
    color_continuous_scale="Viridis",
)

fig_hiv_map.update_layout(height=600)

fig_hiv_map.show()
```

HIV prevalence remains highly concentrated in Southern and Eastern Africa. The long-term trend shows the historical development of the epidemic followed by a period of stabilization and decline, consistent with expanded prevention and treatment efforts, including ART.

# Health expenditure


Health expenditure per capita generally increased over time, although the pattern varies substantially between countries. Greater financial resources can support health-system capacity, including HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and ARV services.

# RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HIV AND HEALTH EXPENDITURE


<div class="interpretation">

The correlation coefficient describes the strength and direction of the linear association between health expenditure per capita and HIV prevalence. It should not be interpreted as evidence that health expenditure causes HIV prevalence to increase or decrease.

<div class="interpretation">

The analysis suggests that the relationship between health expenditure and HIV prevalence is complex rather than simply inverse. Some countries with high HIV prevalence also have relatively high health expenditure because greater spending may reflect substantial investment in managing a large HIV burden.

Countries with lower spending can also have lower prevalence for reasons unrelated to spending, including differences in epidemic history, population structure, prevention, testing, treatment coverage, and other social and health-system factors.

</div> 


# Conclusion 

<div class="conclusion-box"> 

## Key Findings 

This analysis examined HIV prevalence among people aged 15–49 and current health expenditure per capita across countries and over time. 

### 1. HIV burden varies substantially 

HIV prevalence differs considerably between countries, with the highest levels concentrated in Southern and Eastern Africa. This reflects the historical development and geographical concentration of the HIV epidemic. 

### 2. Health expenditure differs widely 

Current health expenditure per capita varies substantially across countries. Higher spending is generally concentrated in wealthier countries, while many low- and middle-income countries operate with considerably fewer resources per person. 

### 3. Health spending and HIV prevalence have a complex relationship 

The analysis does not support a simple conclusion that higher health expenditure automatically results in lower HIV prevalence. Countries with high HIV prevalence may also have high health expenditure because substantial resources are required to provide HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and ARV therapy. 

### 4. Sustained investment remains important 

Continued investment in health systems, HIV prevention, testing, treatment, ARV therapy, and health-system capacity remains important for reducing HIV-related morbidity and improving long-term health outcomes. 

### Limitations 

The analysis is based on observational country-level data. Therefore, the observed relationships should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Differences in epidemic history, socioeconomic conditions, healthcare access, prevention programmes, treatment coverage, and data quality may influence the results.

 </div> 
 
 ## Final Message 
 
 <div class="interpretation"> 
 
 **Overall, the dashboard demonstrates how publicly available health data can be combined with Python to identify patterns in HIV prevalence, health expenditure, and health-system investment. The findings highlight the importance of sustained HIV prevention, treatment, ARV therapy, and broader health-system strengthening.**
